summary: My declared family (sequence-length curriculum) was killed by its own first measurement: training at T=512 instead of 2048 changes step time by 2% at this model size, so there are no free steps to buy there (0.998900 vs 0.997333 baseline). Profiling the input pipeline off-GPU led me to a real but ultimately non-binding fact -- prepare.make_dataloader costs 159ms of CPU per 128x2048 micro-batch -- and my 2.2x faster prefetching replacement measured as a wash at depth 8 (0.988273 vs a3's 0.988763) and -2% throughput at depth 6 (0.983476 vs a4's 0.982903), because next() already overlaps the async backward and the GPU step is 162-175ms. EMA/Polyak tail averaging on an anneal-to-zero schedule was also neutral-to-worse (0.982987 vs a0's 0.982265), and my last run showed the depth-6 width ladder turns over: dim 896 is 0.984560 against dim 768's 0.978654, because tokens seen collapse from ~480M to 295M. What actually moved val_bpb in this cell was step count and model shape (batch 2**18, window 256, shallow+wide to dim 768), all peers' work, which I adopted three times. Next I would test a non-zero final LR paired with a wide averaging window (the one regime where averaging should beat annealing, and the only untested corner of the EMA idea), and MLP expansion ratio at depth 6 / dim 768, which is the cheapest remaining way to trade capacity for steps.
